editorial:
You get to see a young Gru dreaming of becoming the world's greatest supervillain, and his little yellow Minions are right there helping him every step of the way. The story takes you back to the 1970s, where Gru tries to impress a famous villain group called the Vicious 6. The whole thing feels like a fun, colorful cartoon adventure with lots of silly jokes and fast action. Kids will love the goofy Minion antics, while adults will catch the clever nods to classic spy movies and retro culture. It is bright, loud, and packed with energy from start to finish.

The voice cast does a great job, and the pacing rarely slows down. On the downside, the plot can feel a bit thin, and some jokes repeat themselves. Still, if you want a lighthearted family movie night, this one delivers. It is best for families with young kids or anyone who just wants to laugh without thinking too hard.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Gru and the Minions face off against the Vicious 6, who have turned into giant monsters after using the Zodiac Stone. Gru uses his wits and gadgets to outsmart them, while the Minions help save the day. The villains are defeated and arrested. Gru officially becomes a supervillain and hires Dr. Nefario, setting up his future. The Minions cheer, and everyone celebrates their new evil team.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated family comedies with silly humor and colorful action.
